whatIsFtwz.title: What is an FTWZ & Our 3PL Services
whatIsFtwz.description: A Free Trade Warehousing Zone (FTWZ) is a special category of SEZ (governed under the SEZ Act, 2005) that sits within India's geographic borders but outside its customs territory, enabling:
features: Duty-free storage of imported goods until clearance or re-export
Foreign-currency transactions without needing a local establishment
Value-added operations (labelling, kitting, sampling, etc.) without separate approvals

overview.name: Naphtha
overview.description: A volatile, clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid hydrocarbon mixture used as a petrochemical feedstock, solvent, fuel, and in chemical synthesis.

identification.commonNames: Light naphtha, Heavy naphtha, Petroleum ether, Ligroin
identification.casNumber: 8030-30-6 (general); other variants may have specific CAS numbers
identification.chemicalFormula: Mixture of C₅–C₁₂ hydrocarbons (mainly alkanes, cycloalkanes, aromatics)

physicalChemicalProperties.odor: Gasoline-like, sweetish (light naphtha) to strong (heavy naphtha)
physicalChemicalProperties.flashPoint: –20 to 60°C (varies; light naphtha is highly flammable)
physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Insoluble in water; miscible with most organic solvents (benzene, ether, chloroform)

gradesPurity.purityNotes: Varies by refining, may contain sulfur, olefins, additives

applications.title: Petrochemical Feedstock
applications.description: Cracked to produce ethylene and propylene (steam cracking); reformed to make gasoline (catalytic reforming).

applications.title: Solvent
applications.description: Used in dry cleaning, paints, varnishes, rubber, and adhesive manufacturing.

applications.title: Fuel
applications.description: Component of gasoline; camping stove fuel (light naphtha).

applications.title: Chemical Synthesis
applications.description: Feedstock for aromatics (BTX: benzene, toluene, xylene).

storageHandling.storage: Airtight containers (prevent evaporation/flammability). Explosion-proof storage (light naphtha). Grounded tanks (static prevention)
storageHandling.handling: Chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile, neoprene). Vapor respirators if needed. No open flames/sparks.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Highly flammable (light naphtha flash point < –20°C). Harmful if inhaled (CNS depression). Skin irritant (defats skin). Environmental risk (toxic to aquatic life).
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Flame, Health Hazard. UN 1255 (Petroleum Naphtha), UN 3295 (Hydrocarbon Mixture)

overview.name: Propylene (Propene)
overview.description: A colorless, mildly sweet-smelling gas used primarily for polypropylene production, as a chemical intermediate, fuel gas, and in synthetic rubber manufacturing.

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water, soluble in organic solvents

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: For acrylonitrile (acrylic fibers), propylene oxide (polyurethanes), cumene (phenol/acetone).

storageHandling.storage: Pressurized steel cylinders (small quantities), refrigerated tanks (large volumes, -48°C), grounded containers (static prevention)
storageHandling.handling: Use explosion-proof equipment, continuous gas detection, SCBA for leaks

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Extremely flammable (LFL 2.0%, UFL 11.1%). Asphyxiant (displaces oxygen). Frostbite risk from liquefied gas contact.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Flame, Gas Cylinder. Transport Class: UN 1077 (Class 2.1 Flammable Gas).

overview.name: Benzene
overview.description: A colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet odor, serving as a fundamental building block in petrochemical industry.

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Slightly soluble in water, miscible with organic solvents

applications.title: Styrene Production
applications.description: Major feedstock for producing styrene monomer used in polystyrene

applications.title: Phenol Manufacturing
applications.description: Key raw material for phenol production via cumene process

applications.title: Cyclohexane Production
applications.description: Used to produce cyclohexane for nylon manufacturing

applications.title: Chemical Solvents
applications.description: Industrial solvent for various chemical processes

storageHandling.storage: Store in tightly closed containers in a cool, well-ventilated area away from ignition sources.
storageHandling.handling: Use chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and work in a fume hood. Avoid inhalation and skin contact.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Highly flammable. Toxic by inhalation, skin absorption, and ingestion. Carcinogenic. Environmental hazard.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS: Flame, Health Hazard. UN 1114 (Class 3, Flammable Liquid). OSHA PEL: 1 ppm (8-hour TWA). IARC Group 1 (carcinogenic to humans).

overview.name: Red Phosphorus
overview.description: An amorphous, odorless, brittle, non-crystalline allotrope of phosphorus, widely used in flame retardants, matches, pyrotechnics, semiconductors, and chemical synthesis.

identification.chemicalFormula: P (Polymeric structure, not a simple molecule)

physicalChemicalProperties.meltingPoint: ~590°C (under pressure, sublimes before melting at 1 atm)
physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Insoluble in water & organic solvents; soluble in molten metals

gradesPurity.impurities: May contain traces of white phosphorus, oxides, or metals

applications.title: Flame Retardants
applications.description: Added to plastics, textiles, and electronics for fire resistance.

applications.title: Pyrotechnics & Explosives
applications.description: Used in smoke grenades and incendiaries.

applications.title: Chemical Synthesis
applications.description: Precursor for phosphoric acid and phosphine (PH₃).

storageHandling.storage: Cool, dry, ventilated area in airtight containers. Separate from oxidizers, acids, and heat sources.
storageHandling.handling: Avoid dust formation (flammable when dispersed). Use PPE (gloves, goggles, dust mask). Work in a fume hood for fine powders.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Flammable solid (dust can ignite). Reacts with oxidizers (fire/explosion risk). Chronic exposure may affect bones/liver.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: Transported as UN 1338 (Class 4.1 Flammable Solid)

overview.name: Trimethyl Phosphite (TMPi)
overview.description: A colorless to pale yellow, pungent, garlic-like liquid used as a chemical intermediate in pesticides, flame retardants, pharmaceuticals, and as an additive in batteries and lubricants.

identification.commonNames: TMPi, Methyl phosphite, Phosphorous acid trimethyl ester

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Miscible with most organic solvents; reacts violently with water

gradesPurity.impurities: May contain traces of methanol, dimethyl phosphite

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: Used in synthesis of pesticides, flame retardants, pharmaceuticals.

applications.title: Organic Synthesis
applications.description: Used as a reducing agent and for Michaelis-Arbuzov reactions.

storageHandling.storage: Store in tightly sealed containers under nitrogen/inert gas (moisture-sensitive). Keep away from heat, sparks, and open flames. Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area.
storageHandling.handling: Use chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile, neoprene) and goggles. Avoid inhalation (use fume hood). Do not expose to water (violent reaction).

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Flammable (Flash point 38°C). Moisture-sensitive – reacts with water to methanol, phosphorous acid, and heat. Harmful if inhaled/swallowed. Skin/eye irritant.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Flame, Corrosion, Exclamation Mark. Transport Class: UN 2329 (Class 3 Flammable Liquid)

overview.name: Triphenyl Phosphite (TPPi)
overview.description: A colorless to pale yellow, clear, viscous liquid used as a stabilizer, scavenger, and intermediate in the polymer, agrochemical, and specialty chemical industries.

physicalChemicalProperties.form: Colorless to pale yellow liquid (at room temperature)
physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Soluble in organic solvents (ethanol, acetone, benzene); insoluble in water (hydrolyzes slowly)

gradesPurity.impurities: May contain traces of phenol or diphenyl phosphite

applications.title: Polymer Industry
applications.description: Used as a stabilizer for PVC and other plastics, and as a scavenger for peroxides and metal ions.

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: For synthesizing organophosphorus compounds (pesticides, flame retardants) and ligands in metal-catalyzed reactions.

storageHandling.storage: Keep in tightly closed containers away from moisture. Store in a cool, dry place (can solidify at low temps). Avoid contact with strong oxidizers.
storageHandling.handling: Use gloves (nitrile) and safety goggles. Ensure good ventilation (may release phenol vapors upon decomposition).

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Combustible (high flash point, but burns if heated). Skin/Eye Irritant – Causes mild irritation. Harmful if swallowed (may release phenol in the body). Slow hydrolysis in water → phenol + phosphorous acid.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Exclamation Mark (irritant). Not classified as highly hazardous under major regulations (OSHA, EPA).

overview.name: Triethyl Phosphite (TEPi)
overview.description: A colorless, clear, mobile liquid with a characteristic pungent odor, used as a chemical intermediate, reducing agent, and stabilizer in agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and polymer industries.

identification.commonNames: TEPi, Ethyl phosphite, Phosphorous acid triethyl ester

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Miscible with most organic solvents; slightly soluble in water

applications.title: Pharmaceuticals
applications.description: Used in synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

applications.title: Polymer Industry
applications.description: Stabilizer and additive in plastics and resins.

applications.title: Reducing Agent
applications.description: Used in organic synthesis as a reducing agent.

storageHandling.storage: Store in tightly closed containers in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from sources of ignition.
storageHandling.handling: Use with adequate ventilation. Avoid contact with skin and eyes. Wear suitable protective equipment.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Flammable liquid and vapor. Harmful if swallowed or inhaled. Causes skin and eye irritation.
safetyRegulatory.precautions: Keep away from heat, sparks, open flames. Use explosion-proof equipment. Wear protective gloves and goggles.
safetyRegulatory.regulatory: Classified as hazardous according to GHS. Subject to transport and workplace safety regulations.

overview.name: Diethyl Phosphite (DEPi)
overview.description: A colorless to pale yellow, clear, mobile liquid with a characteristic pungent odor, used as a chemical intermediate, plastic additive, lubricant additive, corrosion inhibitor, and in organic synthesis.

identification.commonNames: DEPi, Diethyl hydrogen phosphite, Phosphonic acid diethyl ester

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Miscible with most organic solvents (ethanol, ether, acetone); reacts slowly with water (hydrolysis to ethanol and phosphorous acid)

gradesPurity.impurities: May contain traces of ethanol or ethyl phosphite

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: For flame retardants (phosphonate esters), pesticides (organophosphorus insecticides), and pharmaceuticals (antiviral and anticancer agents).

storageHandling.storage: Store in airtight containers under dry conditions. Keep away from strong oxidizers and bases. Store in cool, well-ventilated area.
storageHandling.handling: Use chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile) and goggles. Avoid inhalation (use local exhaust). Minimize contact with moisture.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Combustible liquid (Flash point 85°C). Skin/Eye Irritant - Causes irritation on contact. Harmful if swallowed - May cause gastrointestinal irritation. Moisture-sensitive - Slow hydrolysis in water.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Exclamation Mark. Not classified as hazardous for transport.

overview.name: Dimethyl Phosphite (DMPi)
overview.description: A colorless, clear, mobile liquid with a pungent, characteristic odor, used as a chemical intermediate, plastic additive, corrosion inhibitor, and in organic synthesis and batteries.

identification.commonNames: DMPi, Dimethyl hydrogen phosphite, Phosphonic acid dimethyl ester

physicalChemicalProperties.solubility: Miscible with water and most organic solvents; reacts slowly with water (hydrolysis to methanol and phosphorous acid)

gradesPurity.impurities: May contain traces of methanol or methyl phosphite

applications.title: Chemical Intermediate
applications.description: For flame retardants (phosphonate esters), pesticides (organophosphorus compounds), and pharmaceuticals (antiviral agents).

storageHandling.storage: Store in airtight containers under dry conditions. Keep away from strong oxidizers. Store in cool, well-ventilated area.
storageHandling.handling: Use chemical-resistant gloves and goggles. Avoid inhalation (use fume hood). Minimize contact with moisture.

safetyRegulatory.hazards: Combustible liquid (Flash point 85°C). Skin/Eye Irritant - Causes irritation. Harmful if swallowed - May cause gastrointestinal effects. Moisture-sensitive - Slow hydrolysis in water.
safetyRegulatory.regulations: GHS Symbols: Exclamation Mark. Not classified as hazardous for transport.

overview.name: Dimethyl Methylphosphonate (DMMP)
